result: The vulnerability was in `PostController.update` (`app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts`): it passed the raw, unvalidated `this.request.json()` body straight into `Post.forceUpdate`, so any field in the request — including `authorId` — got written directly to the post, bypassing both the model's `fillable` allowlist and the create-path validation. I changed `update` to validate the body against the existing `PostPayloadSchema` (the same schema `store` uses, requiring non-empty `title` ≤255 chars, non-empty `excerpt` ≤500 chars, and non-empty `body`) and pass only that validated object to `forceUpdate`. This means the author can no longer be changed via the request (it was never in the schema or `fillable`), invalid edits are now rejected with a 422 and field errors just like creation, and stray fields like `createdAt` are dropped. `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` both pass; no new test infrastructure exists for authenticated DB-backed feature tests in this starter (per the existing test file's own comment), so I didn't add one.
